column1: DENGUE CASE REPORTING During the 40th week, 1240 suspected dengue cases were reported  across  24  districts/regions,  compared to  1216    cases  in  the  previous  week,  reflecting  2%  increase.  The Western Province accounted for 43.2% of total cases, with the  Colombo  Municipal  Council (CMC)  contributing 5.4%, the rest  of  Colombo  District  14.8%,  Gampaha District  17.3%,  and  Kalutara  District  5.6%.  Outside  the Western Province, notable case contributions  were reported  from  Kandy  (12.6%),  Galle  (5.6%),  Ratnapura (4.4%), Matale (4.2%), Kalmunai (4.2%), Kegalle (3.8%), Kurunegala (3.5%),  Matara (3.1%), Jaffna (2.7%), Hambantota  (2.3%),  Batticaloa  (2%)  and  Anuradhapura (2%) (see Table 1) (compared to the previous week, colour of %: red=increase, green=decrease, blue=no change). Previously classified 9 high-risk MOH areas in week 39, were not identified as high-risk in the 40th week of 2026 (Table 2). MIDNIGHT TOTAL OF DENGUE PATIENT ADMISSIONS * After incorporating delayed hospital reports, the average midnight total for the 39th week increased from 435 to 437. In  the  40th  week  of  2026,  the  average  midnight  total  of dengue  patients  across  73  sentinel  hospitals  was  411. Compared to the  previous  week, in the  40th  week,  19 hospitals reported an increase, while 28 reported a decrease.
